description: "DeepCode: Open Agentic Coding (Agent Harness & Loop Engineering & Multi-Agent Orchestration)"

summary.one_liner: DeepCode is an open-source, local Coding Agent (formerly Paper2Code-focused) that works on real repositories through TUI, Desktop, and Web clients sharing one background service.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a Coding Agent that can read and search code, edit files, apply patches, run commands and tests, and continue from the results, with tool calls and file changes kept visible. Goal-driven Loop Engineering lets a natural-language goal keep running through analysis, implementation, verification and repair, and users can add requirements, pause, stop, or resume. Sessions, memory, models, Skills, permissions and Goals are shared across the TUI (`deepcode`), Desktop (`deepcode desktop`) and Web (`deepcode web`) clients via one local service. It also supports MCP servers, Agent Plugins, Automations for recurring tasks, subagents, and Paper2Code for turning papers into code. Much of the README is a dated changelog, which was truncated before the install steps.
use_cases: run a coding agent on a local repository
fix bugs and add tests with an AI agent
automate recurring repo maintenance like test repair
reproduce a research paper as code (Paper2Code)
how_to_run: Install the runtime (see Quick start in the README; the exact install command was not in the truncated text)
deepcode web (open the web workbench in a browser)
notable: TUI, Desktop, and Web clients share one local background service, sessions, and Goals
Goal-driven Loop Engineering with evidence-driven completion and verification
Sandboxed command execution with permissions, hook-file approval, and optional strict command screening
Paper2Code workflow that turns papers and reference repos into implementations
Skills and Agent Plugins compatible with Claude-style and AGENTS.md conventions
caveats: The computer must stay awake for background work, and pending approvals still need a human response (per README)
Several features are opt-in or platform-specific, such as Windows sandbox behaviour and Desktop packaging
Multiple providers and models require user-supplied connections and keys
